title: What is known about 1RB0LA_0RC0RB_1LD1LA_1LC1RE_1RF0RD_1LA---
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0LA_0RC0RB_1LD1LA_1LC1RE_1RF0RD_1LA---.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open, and it is a Collatz-type question. The run is a sequence of phases: a counter n becomes about 3n/2 each phase, and the parity of n edits a short word P on the tape. One word, reached after a particular run of 42 parities, halts. Lean proves the phase rounds for all lengths; the word dynamics is measured by simulation and checked against the real run.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (F1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 59,705 cells have been visited and 33,523 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: fixed/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506).

claims.title: One round of a phase, and whole phases of rounds
claims.text: The round P (10)^(c+2) 111 0^(2g) B>0 → two pairs fewer, six more visited zeros, for every count and every tape beyond (drain), and any number of rounds at once (drain_iter).

claims.title: The phase map agrees with the machine
claims.text: At all 17 transitions between the 19 phase starts of the first 4·10<sup>8</sup> steps (the last at step 235,162,520, n = 13,989) the measured word map predicts the next phase start.

claims.title: A halt is reachable in the word dynamics
claims.text: Exploring every word P for every sequence of parities (1,500 words): from the empty word a halt is reached after 42 phases with parities 1, 0, 1, 0, … (the word counts up like a binary counter), through the word 1111 with n even. Halting transitions are reachable from 26 of the transitions explored.

claims.title: 20,000 phases without a halt
claims.text: From the first phase start (step 161, P = 1, n = 6), computed exactly: no halt in 20,000 phases (n then has 11,704 bits); 23 distinct words, none longer than 8 cells.

claims.title: Halts with probability 1, at an absurd time
claims.text: With random parities the word stays short and keeps returning to the empty word (200 random walks of 2,000 phases: no halt in 400,000 phases). Reaching the halting word needs a specific run of about 42 parities, about one chance in 2<sup>40</sup> per return, so with coin-flip parities the machine halts with probability 1, but after about 2<sup>40</sup> phases, when n has about 10<sup>11</sup> digits.

claims.title: Does it halt from blank tape?
claims.text: It halts if and only if the parities of the 3/2 counter ever spell out one of the halting runs of the word dynamics: a Collatz-type question.

sections.heading: Phases: a counter and a word
html: Stop the machine every time the head, in state B, is at the right end of the tape with the tape reading

a word P, a run of n pairs and the block 111. During a phase the head bounces between the block and the far end: each round it takes two pairs and comes back six cells further, so the visited part grows into a long run of zeros. When one or no pair is left the head reaches P, edits it, and on the way back turns the zeros into the next run of pairs: n becomes about 3n/2 (3n/2 + d for even n, (3n + d)/2 for odd n, with d between 3 and 17 depending on P).

So the counter follows a 3/2 map like Antihydra, and its parity at the end of each phase is fed into the word P: from the empty word an odd n writes 1, an even n then appends 000, and so on: alternating parities make P count up like a binary counter.

sections.heading: A halting word
html: Exploring the word dynamics for all parity sequences shows that the word 1111 halts the machine when the next n is even (and a few other words do too). The shortest way to get there from the empty word is 42 phases with the parities 1, 0, 1, 0, … and a few others in a precise order: the word has to count far enough without being reset.

The real orbit is driven by the parities of the 3/2 counter, which look random. Computed exactly for 20,000 phases (n then has 11,704 binary digits) it never halts, and the word never gets longer than 8 cells. With random parities the word keeps returning to empty, and the precise run of 42 needed has a chance of about 2−40 each time, so the machine would halt with probability 1, but only after about 240 phases. Deciding it means understanding the parities of a 3/2 map: the Antihydra obstacle.

Related machines. 1RB---_0RC0RB_1LD1LE_1LC1RF_1RB0LE_1RA0RD, 1RB---_1LC0RB_0LD0LC_1RE1RB_1RD1LF_1LA0LE and 1RB0LA_0RC0RB_1LD1LA_1LC1RE_1RF0RD_1LA--- share this core. The second is the third mirrored and relabelled (the same table, started in another state); the first differs from the third in one transition that is used only at a few phase ends. Their word maps agree on all 400 words compared (both parities), except two transitions of the first (from 11111 and 1111011), and all three reach a halt by the same 42-phase route; their orbits differ because they start differently.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape stopped growing in the second half of the run (bounded so far, or growing so slowly that no record fell in the last half). Right of the start it grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.506).
After 109 steps the tape spans 59,705 cells (26 left of the start, 44,238 right), with a density of 1s of 0.561.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

summary: Antihydra-like 3/2 map with a word counter: each phase multiplies n by 3/2 and its parity edits a word P; a halt is reachable but only after a specific run of 42 parities (none in 20,000 phases).
